Text: $SOUN Quick peek into my approach and why i am so confident even if structures are invalidated? Wyckoff is not a strategy in general its an approach that combines fundamentals with technical analysis ( created more than 100 years ago). Wyckoff spent years researching price action when money flows in. Wyckoff structures are basically footprints that institutions create when they pouring money in. Wyckoff realised that the chart is acting specific way when massive buy/sell order comes in. Example- investor X makes purchase of desired stock. Even if his stake is big, it doesn't necessarily means that the stock goes up, instead it starts positioning itself the way that make it possible for stock to change direction(consolidate). That range creates possible major accumulation. Within that range investor N ( now also other investors notices-V,I,D,I,A) keep investing. That creates minor accumulations. You can see 10 of them and it might not be enough to send the stock up. But....

Text: $SOUN The total cost to carry a short position in SoundHound AI (SOUN) has two main components: 1. Borrow Fee (share loan rate) This fluctuates a lot. The most recent data (mid-October 2026) puts it at roughly 2.54% annualized, down from a 5–7% range in early September and a peak near 58–61% in May 2026. It was around 13% in early August and 17.7% in early June. The rate is driven by how tight the borrow market is — SOUN has had 0% share availability for extended stretches, which pushes rates up. 2. Margin Interest Rate This is the interest your broker charges on the cash collateral in your margin account. It's typically around 8–9% annualized at most major brokers (e.g., Interactive Brokers, Fidelity, Schwab), and varies by account tier and balance. So in total, a short SOUN position currently costs roughly ~10–12% per year in carry (borrow + margin interest), though that number swings wildly with the borrow rate.
